newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish share rally seen continuing on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Danish share rally seen continuing on Tuesday.

text.p: Danish shares on Monday clawed back about half of the losses incurred after Friday's warning to markets by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan and dealers expected upward movement to continue on Tuesday.
"Today's rises are a reaction to Friday's fall which was a little excessive. Sentiment in the market is still positive so we shall probably continue up a little tomorrow," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.24 point up, at 130.60, in overall bourse turnover of 426.5 million crowns.
The KFX December future rose 0.45 point to 129.65 with 295 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns, traded.
The KFX fell 2.38 point on Friday after Greenspan warned against "irrational exuberance" in securities markets.
Brewing group Carlsberg was unaffected by a British government decision to refer to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission a planned takeover of British joint venture Carlsberg-Tetley by Bass Plc.

The Danish parent's share closed one crown up at 378 crowns, in turnover of 32,000 trades although dealers said they expected the share to be regarded with some uncertainty pending the commission's decision, expected next March.
Radiometer gained five crowns, to 370, despite analysts' expectations that its first-half 1996/97 results -- due on Wednesday -- would show virtually flat earnings.
